question: Does the sh5 release false onset follow the actual command/sensor trajectory, or the shared observer's nominal payload-COM history?
capture: Run the unchanged exposed sh5 stock episode once with R16 balanced/early-information control and once with R17 later-information control. A detector wrapper records only its documented 6000 per-tick inputs, physical payload declaration, and the public controller-derived nominal payload COM already installed before that tick. It does not store or read simulated contact or external force truth.
factorial: Replay each complete input stream through a new isolated shared estimator against each complete nominal COM schedule, yielding sensor16/model16, sensor16/model17, sensor17/model16, sensor17/model17. The wrong controller is never advanced. Each replay installs only the other recorded causal COM schedule in the otherwise identical public nominal model. Exact diagonal equality is required for returned residual, wrench, table projection, fast innovation, scores, counters and decisions on all 6000 ticks.
interpretation: A factor is causal only if swapping that factor changes the release score/decision while holding the other frozen. If the two model schedules are identical, report that the requested model factor does not exist rather than inventing a swap. If both cross cells follow the sensor stream, actual input history suffices. If both follow model schedule, model history suffices. An interaction is reported without assigning a main-factor repair.
repair_gate: No repair is attempted unless a unique causal controller-observable mapping follows from this factorial. Any repair must be frozen before testing separate already-known sham/forced conditions at or near release, without freezing, silencing or resetting detector decisions. No protected or new cases open before a normal screen passes.
limits: No force truth, hidden plant state, detector threshold, grip timing, previous lane mutation, new dependency, hardware or remote operation. Private full traces stay in local evidence.
